GOFAI): its knowledge is an inspectable [semantic network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantic_network) of human-readable links rather than hidden neural weights. The [associative technology stack guide](docs/associative-tech-stack.md) links every component and distinguishes direct runtime dependencies from architecture and development tooling. The case study in [docs/case-studies/issue-451](docs/case-studies/issue-451/README.md) maps the field's best practices onto this associative stack; the design study in [docs/case-studies/issue-649](docs/case-studies/issue-649/README.md) audits how the same stack expresses symbolic **world models** — a current-state and target-state context, their difference, context merge/split, and predicting the consequences of an action, all as links networks rather than embeddings; and the study in [docs/case-studies/issue-686](docs/case-studies/issue-686/README.md) adds **usage-weighted persistence** of meta-language expressions — counting reads and writes and incoming/outgoing link degree so the most used, most changed, and most connected knowledge persists longest, all as a links network.\n\nThe current implementation covers the surface area requested in issue #1:\n\n- library API for symbolic prompt handling\n- CLI chat command\n- HTTP API server with protocol namespaces under `/api/openai/v1`,\n  `/api/anthropic/v1`, `/api/gemini/v1beta`, and `/api/vertex/v1`\n- Telegram bot CLI with long polling by default and an opt-in webhook server, configured through [`lino-arguments`](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments)\n- human-readable Links Notation knowledge and dataset export through `lino-objects-codec`\n- Prepared Docker-in-Docker Telegram bot image published as `ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai:latest` and based on `konard/box-dind:2.1.1`\n- GitHub Pages markdown chat demo backed by a Rust-generated WebAssembly worker\n- Electron desktop shell that starts the local Rust HTTP API and reuses the web chat\n- VS Code extension (desktop **and** web/`vscode.dev`) that embeds the same chat in a Webview around the same HTTP/web boundary\n\nProject direction is tracked in [VISION.md](VISION.md), [GOALS.md](GOALS.md), and [NON-GOALS.md](NON-GOALS.md). The design theses behind its linked transformation model are separated from mathematical and implementation claims in [docs/philosophy.md](docs/philosophy.md). Who the project is for, what pain it closes, and the concrete user journeys it supports today (plus the ones it could support next) are documented in [docs/USER-JOURNEYS.md](docs/USER-JOURNEYS.md). Implementation progress against the vision is tracked in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). The issue #12 synthesis is in [docs/case-studies/issue-12/README.md](docs/case-studies/issue-12/README.md).\n\nLegal and provenance guidance starts with [LEGAL-COMPLIANCE.md](LEGAL-COMPLIANCE.md). Focused guides explain the [Formal AI/language-model boundary](docs/legal/formal-ai-and-language-models.md), [public-domain dedication of AI-assisted output](docs/legal/public-domain-output.md), [candidate datasets](docs/legal/compatible-datasets.md), and [candidate locally transformable or distillable model families](docs/legal/distillable-models.md). Those dated matrices are source-review queues, not approvals; the machine-readable training registry remains authoritative.\n\n## Install\n\nFor one end-to-end reference covering every client, runtime mode, tool,\nmemory/API setting, transcript location, language, and user surface, start with\nthe **[Configuration guide](docs/configuration/README.md)**.\n\nComplete agentic transcript capture, JSON/Links Notation export, OpenCode\nSQLite extraction, and redaction guidance are covered in\n**[Output and session debugging](docs/configuration/output-sessions.md)**.\n\nEvery interface has a dedicated landing page on the\n[site](https://link-assistant.github.io/formal-ai/) with copy-paste install\ninstructions, and a single universal installer covers all of them. The script is\npublished at [`scripts/install.sh`](scripts/install.sh) (POSIX `sh`, for\nmacOS/Linux) and [`scripts/install.ps1`](scripts/install.ps1) (PowerShell, for\nWindows). [2026-08-10T22:06:17.647Z] [INFO]         "content": "# Contributing to formal-ai\n\nThank you for your interest in contributing! This document provides guidelines and instructions for contributing to this project.\n\n## How we develop Formal AI: drive the Agent CLI, never defer\n\n**From issue #538 forward, this is the only way we develop the Formal AI\nsystem.** We do not solve a task by editing code and data by hand and we do not\nsolve it partway and defer the rest to a roadmap. We solve it by **driving Formal\nAI through its own [Agent CLI](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent)** (the\nin-repo agentic driver in `src/agentic_coding/`, running against the\nOpenAI-compatible `formal-ai serve` server), and we get *every* requirement done\nin the same pull request.\n\nThis section is the development policy and target workflow, not a claim that\nthe repository is already autonomously self-coded. When an existing tool gap\nforces a manual tool extension, record that boundary plainly, retry a smallest\nleaf through Formal AI, and measure only genuinely session-authored lines. A\nreviewed task decomposition must name its smallest leaves; the acceptance floor\nis at least one real Formal-AI/Agent-CLI-authored leaf out of every five (20%),\nwith a captured session and paired commit trailers. Raise that measured share\nover time; never relabel manual work as self-authored.\n\nConcretely, every change must follow these rules:\n\n1. **The tool authors the change, not you.** Drive the Agent CLI + Formal AI to\n   produce the change. Where the output lands in the repo (e.g. seed data), a\n   test must assert that the committed artifact is **byte-for-byte** what the\n   Agent-CLI-driven recipe produces, so the tool — not a hand-edit — is the\n   author and cannot silently regress. See the issue #538 case study\n   ([`docs/case-studies/issue-538/`](docs/case-studies/issue-538/)) for the\n   pattern and the committed `agent-cli-session*.json` sessions.\n2. **No pre-emptive deferral, no refusals, no follow-ups.** \"This is large or\n   hard\" is never a reason to ship a slice and route the rest to a roadmap. Find\n   the smallest real, tested, reproducible slice of *each* requirement and\n   execute it now, in this PR. Read\n   [`docs/case-studies/issue-538/refusal-anti-pattern.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-538/refusal-anti-pattern.md)\n   before opening a PR — it is the failed reasoning we do not repeat, and we do\n   not teach Formal AI to refuse or defer like that.\n3. **When the tool can't do it, extend the tool, then retry.** Falling back to a\n   manual edit is allowed only after you have proven the Agent CLI / Formal AI\n   cannot yet do it — and then you must immediately improve the Agent CLI /\n   Formal AI so it *can* in general, and re-run through the tool.\n4. **Prove generality with different words each time.** Use a *different* natural\n   language request for each case so a passing run proves the solution is truly\n   general, not hardcoded to one phrasing (issue #538 drives tomato and potato\n   with two differently-worded requests).\n5. **Report faithfully.** State what is done and verified plainly. Honesty means\n   reporting results accurately; it is never a license to stop early or to dress\n   a refusal as an \"honest scope\" section.\n6. **Real Agent-CLI E2E tests in CI, plus a per-requirement test and a\n   whole-task test.** Every change that touches the agentic path must add (or\n   update) a real end-to-end test that boots `formal-ai serve` and drives it\n   with the actual `@link-assistant/agent` CLI over the OpenAI-compatible\n   endpoint — no mocks or in-process shortcuts. Keep the round-trip green in CI\n   (see `test-agent-cli-e2e` in `.github/workflows/release.yml` and the driver\n   script `experiments/agent_cli_e2e/run_agent_cli.sh`). In addition, ship one\n   unit/integration test **per requirement in the issue** and one test that\n   exercises the **whole task** end-to-end so a regression on any single\n   requirement — or on the composition of all of them — breaks the build.\n7. **Hardcoded cases only in tests; production code stays general.** A test may\n   hardcode inputs and expected outputs (that is what a test is *for*), but the\n   engine, planner, seed loader, and Agent-CLI-driven recipes never branch on a\n   specific concept, phrase, or URL. If the only way to make a green case pass\n   is a match-on-literal in `src/`, extend the general routing table (`concept\n   registry`, `capability classifier`, `plan_chat_step`) so future concepts get\n   the same treatment for free.\n8. **Real logs in the case study, not synthesized ones.** When a case study\n   claims the Agent CLI drove the change, it must ship the real captured log of\n   the round-trip (see `docs/case-studies/issue-538/agent-cli-e2e-run.log`), and\n   the committed session JSON must be reproducible byte-for-byte by\n   `cargo test`.\n9. **Commit in small, atomic steps.** Every commit should be independently\n   useful and reviewable — one logical change per commit, buildable in\n   isolation. Interrupted work stays preserved in the PR because each commit\n   already stands on its own; do not batch a day of unrelated edits into one\n   commit.\n\n### Testing external agentic CLIs\n\nWhen validating `codex`, `opencode`, `gemini`, or the `agent` CLI against a\nlocal Formal AI server, follow\n[`docs/testing/agentic-cli-tools.md`](docs/testing/agentic-cli-tools.md). The\nguide defines the fixture markers, logging proxy assertions, phrasing matrices,\nand CI shape needed to prove that a result came from Formal AI and that the\nclient actually executed the expected tools.\n\n### Spawn a reference assistant when you need a natural-language target\n\nWhen a change is about *how Formal AI talks* to the user — narration before a\ntool runs, an error explanation, the wording of a question — it helps to see how\na strong conversational assistant would phrase the same step. This document provides guidelines and instructions for contributing to this project.\n\n## How we develop Formal AI: drive the Agent CLI, never defer\n\n**From issue #538 forward, this is the only way we develop the Formal AI\nsystem.** We do not solve a task by editing code and data by hand and we do not\nsolve it partway and defer the rest to a roadmap. We solve it by **driving Formal\nAI through its own [Agent CLI](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent)** (the\nin-repo agentic driver in `src/agentic_coding/`, running against the\nOpenAI-compatible `formal-ai serve` server), and we get *every* requirement done\nin the same pull request.\n\nThis section is the development policy and target workflow, not a claim that\nthe repository is already autonomously self-coded. When an existing tool gap\nforces a manual tool extension, record that boundary plainly, retry a smallest\nleaf through Formal AI, and measure only genuinely session-authored lines. A\nreviewed task decomposition must name its smallest leaves; the acceptance floor\nis at least one real Formal-AI/Agent-CLI-authored leaf out of every five (20%),\nwith a captured session and paired commit trailers. Raise that measured share\nover time; never relabel manual work as self-authored.\n\nConcretely, every change must follow these rules:\n\n1. **The tool authors the change, not you.** Drive the Agent CLI + Formal AI to\n   produce the change. Where the output lands in the repo (e.g. seed data), a\n   test must assert that the committed artifact is **byte-for-byte** what the\n   Agent-CLI-driven recipe produces, so the tool — not a hand-edit — is the\n   author and cannot silently regress. See the issue #538 case study\n   ([`docs/case-studies/issue-538/`](docs/case-studies/issue-538/)) for the\n   pattern and the committed `agent-cli-session*.json` sessions.\n2. **No pre-emptive deferral, no refusals, no follow-ups.** \"This is large or\n   hard\" is never a reason to ship a slice and route the rest to a roadmap. Find\n   the smallest real, tested, reproducible slice of *each* requirement and\n   execute it now, in this PR. Read\n   [`docs/case-studies/issue-538/refusal-anti-pattern.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-538/refusal-anti-pattern.md)\n   before opening a PR — it is the failed reasoning we do not repeat, and we do\n   not teach Formal AI to refuse or defer like that.\n3. **When the tool can't do it, extend the tool, then retry.** Falling back to a\n   manual edit is allowed only after you have proven the Agent CLI / Formal AI\n   cannot yet do it — and then you must immediately improve the Agent CLI /\n   Formal AI so it *can* in general, and re-run through the tool.\n4. **Prove generality with different words each time.** Use a *different* natural\n   language request for each case so a passing run proves the solution is truly\n   general, not hardcoded to one phrasing (issue #538 drives tomato and potato\n   with two differently-worded requests).\n5. **Report faithfully.** State what is done and verified plainly. Honesty means\n   reporting results accurately; it is never a license to stop early or to dress\n   a refusal as an \"honest scope\" section.\n6. **Real Agent-CLI E2E tests in CI, plus a per-requirement test and a\n   whole-task test.** Every change that touches the agentic path must add (or\n   update) a real end-to-end test that boots `formal-ai serve` and drives it\n   with the actual `@link-assistant/agent` CLI over the OpenAI-compatible\n   endpoint — no mocks or in-process shortcuts. In addition, ship one\n   unit/integration test **per requirement in the issue** and one test that\n   exercises the **whole task** end-to-end so a regression on any single\n   requirement — or on the composition of all of them — breaks the build.\n7. **Hardcoded cases only in tests; production code stays general.** A test may\n   hardcode inputs and expected outputs (that is what a test is *for*), but the\n   engine, planner, seed loader, and Agent-CLI-driven recipes never branch on a\n   specific concept, phrase, or URL. extending `scripts/check-file-size.rs` and adding unit coverage that parses and bounds every checked-in `.lino` file. |\n\n## Current Scope Boundary\n\nThis PR is a deterministic symbolic [2026-08-10T22:10:42.997Z] [INFO]         "content": "# Vision\n\nFormal AI should become a symbolic assistant whose live state is an associative operational space. The assistant should not be defined by hidden neural weights or by a large memoized answer table. It should be defined by an inspectable associative network of links: user messages, source data, inferred meanings, commands, test results, generated code, failures, permissions, and final answers.\n\nThe associative network is the AI. The runtime should activate, extend, query, and simplify that network as work happens.\n\nThe fact-checked design theses behind “AI = data + algorithm,” “everything is a\nlink,” transformation networks, controlled self-modification, recursive\ndecomposition, and Markov substitution are in\n[`docs/philosophy.md`](docs/philosophy.md). That guide distinguishes metaphor,\nmathematical fact, implemented behavior, and target behavior.\n\nThis places Formal AI squarely in the tradition of [symbolic artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbolic_artificial_intelligence) (GOFAI): the link network is a [semantic network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantic_network) in the classical sense, and intelligence is the rule-driven manipulation of human-readable symbols ([physical symbol system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_symbol_system) hypothesis, Newell & Simon 1976) rather than numeric optimization of hidden weights. The audit in [`docs/case-studies/issue-451/symbolic-ai-best-practices.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-451/symbolic-ai-best-practices.md) maps each of the field's best practices onto this associative stack.\n\n## Who This Is For And What Pain It Closes\n\nBefore the architecture, the people. Mainstream AI assistants share a cluster of\npains: you cannot see *why* an answer was produced, the same prompt is not\nguaranteed to return the same answer, useful answers require a GPU and a vendor's\ncloud, the assistant's memory is an opaque store you cannot export or move, and\nyou cannot teach it by editing data instead of retraining weights.\n\nFormal AI is for the person who needs the opposite of each: a **defensible,\nreproducible, ownable, editable** answer. The auditor who must cite reasoning,\nthe multilingual user who wants `en | ru | hi | zh` treated equally, the learner\nwho wants honest execution notes on generated code, the analyst who needs math\nand currency with shown work, the integrator who wants a drop-in\nOpenAI-compatible endpoint with no GPU bill, the privacy-conscious owner who\nexports everything the agent saw and did as one file, and the tinkerer who\nreconfigures behavior by editing seed data.\n\nA concrete example user journey — Dana the auditor asks `What is 8% of $50?`,\ngets `$4`, then asks `Why did you answer that?` and receives the recorded\nimpulse, formalization, decomposition, validation, and simplification that\nproduced it — is walked end to end in\n[`docs/USER-JOURNEYS.md`](docs/USER-JOURNEYS.md). That document enumerates\n**every user journey supported today and every journey we could support next**,\nmapped to the surfaces below and to the principles in this file, so the vision\nmakes a concrete promise rather than only describing the machine.\n\n## Core Idea\n\nThe system should prefer deep understanding of user needs, intent, context, and available evidence over answer memoization. A prompt should trigger enough data collection and reasoning to justify the response for that prompt. What the system learns along the way should remain available as reviewable knowledge, with source links and execution traces attached.\n\nThe default native store is link-native:\n\n- `doublets-rs` is the default native Links Data Store for meanings, history, rules, traces, and executable associations.\n- `doublets-web` / IndexedDB is the browser-side storage shape.\n- Links Notation is the reviewable text format for seed data, portable packages, traces, and repository data.\n- Doublet links are the primitive storage model for this project.\n- `lino-objects-codec` remains useful for converting structured objects into reviewable Links Notation during the transition.\n\nThe dynamic type system should be expressible with doublets:\n\n```text\nType -> SubType\nSubType -> SubType\nSubType -> Value\n```\n\n===GOALS===\n# Goals\n\nThis project should build a practical, inspectable symbolic assistant before it grows into a larger associative intelligence system.\n\n## Architecture Goals\n\n- Maintain the smallest useful seed dataset, then learn or import missing knowledge on demand.\n- Store meanings, events, traces, requirements, handlers, and answer evidence in a link-native form.\n- Use doublet links and Links Notation as the preferred representation for reviewable knowledge.\n- Keep the dynamic type system small enough to understand and flexible enough to grow.\n- Make transparent reasoning a default property of the system, not a diagnostics afterthought.\n- Preserve add-only history for user messages, assistant actions, external data accesses, edits, and state projections.\n- Support reusable associative packages for datasets, skills, substitution rules, and executable handlers.\n- Keep JavaScript as interfacing glue and JSX UI only; compile all logic from Rust (native on servers, WebAssembly in the web app) and reuse the same WASM engine across desktop and editor surfaces.\n\n## Product Goals\n\n- Keep chat-first interaction as the default user experience.\n- Support both ordinary chat mode and explicit agent mode.\n- Keep all public interfaces backed by the same symbolic core: Rust library, CLI, HTTP API, Docker service, GitHub Pages demo, Telegram, and future desktop mode.\n- Provide clear feedback when generated code was compiled, run, not run, or cannot be run in the current environment.\n- Support isolated execution for generated code and agent actions through Docker, server sandboxes, or browser-local VM technology where practical.\n- Let users inspect relevant links visually when chat is not enough.\n- Let users report, correct, add, update, and delete knowledge through natural language while preserving history.\n\n## Reasoning Goals\n\n- Convert each user message into traceable requirements, source events, and candidate meanings.\n- Search local associative knowledge first and external sources only when local knowledge is insufficient.\n- Cache external source access with provenance and refresh policy rather than treating the web as untracked context.\n- Split hard tasks recursively into smaller tasks that can be tested, executed, or answered.\n- Learn from failed code generation, failed tests, timeouts, and review comments.\n- Translate between natural languages, programming languages, and Links Notation as a language of meaning.\n- Reduce contradictions by splitting overloaded names into distinct meanings when needed.\n\n## Universal Solver Goals\n\n- Run the same universal problem-solving algorithm for every request: greetings, identity questions, code generation, translation, source checking, math, and agent actions. The shape of the loop should not branch by domain.\n- Treat formalization, decomposition, candidate generation, validation, and simplification as first-class steps that always run, even when the answer is trivially known.\n- Generate at least one executable test or constraint check per requirement before committing to an answer, following test-driven development.",

Issue #838 was filed by a single `format!` heredoc: it created two temporary\n//! files, exported a context, `printf`-ed one intro line, appended\n//! `tail -c 12000` of the export and called `gh issue create`. Nothing in that\n//! string could be tested, and every command in it was assumed to exist.\n//!\n//! This builder replaces the heredoc with a small, inspectable structure: each\n//! step names the program it needs, every named program is checked with\n//! `command -v` before the first step runs, and a report that wants scratch\n//! files gets one directory that is removed on exit. The report body itself is\n//! no longer assembled in shell — `formal-ai report body` renders it.\n\nuse crate::seed;\n\nconst COMMAND_PLACEHOLDER: &str = \"{command}\";\nconst MESSAGE_PLACEHOLDER: &str = \"{message}\";\n/// Abort the whole script when a required program is missing, instead of\n/// filing a partial report (#839, §7).\nconst PREFLIGHT: &str =\n    \"command -v {command} >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf '%s\\\\n' {message} >&2; exit 1; }\";\n/// Fail on the first error and on an unset variable.\nconst STRICT_MODE: &str = \"set -eu\";\n/// Shell variable holding the scratch directory of one report.\nconst SCRATCH_VARIABLE: &str = \"report_dir\";\n/// One directory per report, removed however the script ends.\n///\n/// GNU `mktemp` only substitutes a trailing run of `X`s, so the suffixed\n/// template of #838 produced the literal name `formal-ai-report.XXXXXX.lino`\n/// in the filed gist. Structured values use a\nJSON code fence rather than leaking a raw protocol envelope:\n\n```json\n{\"status\":\"ok\",\"items\":[\"a\",\"b\"]}\n```\n\nTool results are retained byte-for-byte in the client conversation, then\nnormalized into a localized friendly answer. A follow-up can therefore request\na particular line, URL, or the complete result without losing the transcript.\n\n## Software-authoring completion records\n\nFor one-shot software-authoring requests, `formal-ai with` emits each child\nstdout value as one compact JSON line. Pretty-printed, concatenated, and\nplain-text child output is normalized without putting multi-line values on\nstdout. The final line is owned by Formal AI:\n\n```json\n{\"attempts\":1,\"completion_state\":\"complete\",\"observable_postcondition\":{\"expected\":true,\"kind\":\"workspace_effect\",\"observed\":true,\"paths\":[\"Hello.scala\"]},\"rawMetadata\":{\"formalai\":{\"actual_endpoint\":null,\"endpoint\":\"http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/openai/v1\",\"input_tokens\":15186,\"model\":\"formal-ai\",\"output_tokens\":1553}},\"recovery\":{\"ledger\":\"/home/user/.local/state/formal-ai/completion-recovery.lino\",\"max_attempts\":4,\"strategies_available\":[\"restate_postcondition\",\"name_target_artifact\",\"decompose_into_leaf\"],\"strategies_spent\":[]},\"reason\":\"workspace_effect_observed\",\"type\":\"formal_ai_completion\"}\n```\n\n`complete` requires a non-scratch workspace effect. `incomplete` means the\nclient exited successfully but still produced no effect after the seeded\nladder of bounded corrective attempts. `failed` covers client failure and endpoint mismatch.\n`attempts` makes recovery visible to callers. Token fields are populated from\nthe supported clients' direct, nested, or JSON-string usage envelopes; the\nconfigured model and protocol endpoint are always present. If client output\nnames a conflicting public vendor endpoint, `actual_endpoint` records it and\nthe wrapper exits nonzero.\n\nAfter `formal-ai with` exits, it reports only the session artifact created or\nchanged by that run and prints a resume command where supported. Links Notation is the default so messages, tool calls,\ntool results, metadata, and server exchanges remain readable without losing\ntheir native repeated sequence structure.\n\nStart a server with complete dialog logging before reproducing the problem:\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p dialog-logs\nFORMAL_AI_DIALOG_LOG_DIR=./dialog-logs formal-ai serve --agent-mode\n```\n\nPass `X-Formal-AI-Dialog-ID` from the client when a stable identifier is useful:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/openai/v1/chat/completions \\\n  -H 'content-type: application/json' \\\n  -H 'X-Formal-AI-Dialog-ID: checkout-reproduction' \\\n  -d '{\"model\":\"formal-ai\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Reproduce it\"}]}'\n```\n\nExport that dialog locally:\n\n```bash\nformal-ai context export \\\n  --session checkout-reproduction \\\n  --source both \\\n  --log-dir ./dialog-logs \\\n  --output checkout-reproduction.lino\n```\n\nUse `--format json` only when another program needs JSON:\n\n```bash\nformal-ai context export \\\n  --session checkout-reproduction \\\n  --source both \\\n  --log-dir ./dialog-logs \\\n  --format json \\\n  --output checkout-reproduction.json\n```\n\nThe global diagnostic default is verbose. The stable session/dialog id selects\none server JSONL file or one OpenCode session. Many clients resend the entire conversation on each request, while\nothers send only the newest turn. The exporter finds the largest exact overlap\nbetween the transcript suffix and incoming history prefix. This retains\nincremental turns and avoids duplicating cumulative histories.\n\nResponse extraction understands the protocol envelopes served by Formal AI:\n\n- OpenAI Chat Completions `choices[].message`;\n- OpenAI Responses `output[]` message items, excluding reasoning metadata;\n- Gemini `candidates[].content`;\n- direct objects carrying `role` and `content`;\n- streamed Chat Completions SSE deltas, including fragmented content and\n  indexed, fragmented tool calls.\n\nThe raw request and response bodies remain available in `server_logs` even\nwhen a future response envelope cannot yet be reconstructed as messages.\nConsequently, protocol evidence is not discarded when transcript normalization\ndoes not recognize a vendor-specific field.\n\n### Links Notation conversion contract\n\nThe same Rust serializer handles server dialogs, OpenCode extraction, and\narbitrary JSON. This keeps quoting and sequence behavior identical across every\nentry point.\n\nRecord arrays use native repeated singular keys:\n\n```text\nmessages\n  message\n    role user\n    content \"a:b\"\n  message\n    role assistant\n    content complete\n```\n\nScalar arrays stay inline. Unsafe object keys become explicit `field`, `name`,\nand `value` nodes. Strings that could be confused with `true`, `false`, `null`,\nor a number are quoted. Strings containing both quote styles use a tagged\n`b64:` value, and carriage returns, newlines, and tabs stay on one physical\nLinks Notation line through escaping.\n\nConvert any JSON document with that same implementation:\n\n```bash\nformal-ai context json-to-lino --path request.json --output request.lino\nprintf '%s\\n' '{\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"a:b\"}]}' \\\n  | formal-ai --silent context json-to-lino\n```\n\n### OpenCode SQLite sessions\n\nOpenCode stores sessions under `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/opencode/opencode.db`.\nThe extractor opens the database with SQLite `mode=ro` and orders messages and\nparts by `(time_created, id)` for deterministic output. It first produces a\nstructured JSON tree; the Formal AI CLI then applies the shared Rust serializer\nfor Links Notation output.\n\n```bash\nformal-ai context export \\\n  --session ses_XXXX \\\n  --source opencode \\\n  --db ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \\\n  --output opencode-session.lino\n```\n\nThe export includes session columns, decoded JSON metadata, every message,\nevery part, roles, timestamps, token/cost data, and tool state. The database is\nnever migrated or modified by this command.\n\n### Reporting and privacy\n\nA complete context can contain system prompts, credentials printed by tools,\nsource code, filesystem paths, and model responses. Inspect the local `.lino`\nor `.json` file and redact secrets before attaching it to an issue. Prefer a\nprivate upload when the remaining reproduction is still sensitive.\n\nThe agentic `Report` flow asks twice before acting: first where to report, then\nwhich context to include. .any(|form| {\n            let needle = form.text.to_lowercase();\n            let Some(start) = lower.find(&needle) else {\n                return false;\n            };\n            if seed::localized_response(intent, language)\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| intent.to_owned())\n        .replace(TARGET_PLACEHOLDER, target)\n}\n\n/// Whether `lower` (an already-lowercased request) is a One\n/// parser for classification and composition cannot drift into claiming an\n/// operation that the planner is unable to execute.\n#[must_use]\npub(crate) fn has_file_write_intent(lower: &str) -> bool {\n    parse_write_request(lower).is_some()\n}\n\n/// Whether a request explicitly marks its recovered payload as authoritative\n/// literal bytes rather than a description of another workspace operation.\n///\n/// The marker is seed-backed and multilingual. Resolve it\n    // before the research recipe so requests such as \"tell me about URL\" fetch\n    // that page instead of turning the URL itself into a search query.\n    if let Some(plan) = intent_router::plan_web_fetch_step(&task, messages, tool_names) {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    if let Some(query) = web_research::web_research_query_for(messages) {\n        if let Some(plan) = web_research::plan_web_research_step(messages, tool_names, &query) {\n            return Some(plan);\n        }\n    }\n    if let Some(plan) = intent_router::plan_web_search_step(&task, messages, tool_names) {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    // A generic localized \"find\" cue can describe either an open-web lookup or\n    // a workspace grep. The research routers above get first refusal whenever\n    // the client exposes their tools; explicit local/repository searches were\n    // already claimed by the capability router. This fallback therefore keeps\n    // grep available to grep-only clients without letting an alphabetically\n    // earlier local tool steal a web-research request.\n    if !tool_result::has_latest_turn_result(messages) {\n        if let Some(query) = shell_command::code_search_query_for_task(&task) {\n            if let Some(tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Grep) {\n                return Some(plan_one(\n                    tool,\n                    json!({ \"query\": query, \"pattern\": query }).to_string(),\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    if web_research::has_successful_search_result(messages) {\n        if let Some(query) = web_research::unresolved_web_research_query_for(messages) {\n            if let Some(plan) = web_research::plan_web_research_step(messages, tool_names, &query) {\n                return Some(plan);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    if let Some(answer) = tool_result::latest_turn_answer(messages, tool_names, &task) {\n        return Some(AgenticPlan::Final(answer));\n    }\n    if let Some(plan) = compose_general_change_plan(&task)\n        .map(|plan| plan_general_change_step(messages, tool_names, &plan))\n    {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    if let Some(query) = web_research::unresolved_web_research_query_for(messages) {\n        if let Some(plan) = web_research::plan_web_research_step(messages, tool_names, &query) {\n            return Some(plan);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Run a shell command through the client-owned tool loop, then present its result.\nfn plan_shell_step(messages: &[ChatMessage], tool_names: &[&str], command: &str) -> AgenticPlan {\n    let progress = Progress::scan(messages);\n    if progress.done(Capability::Run) {\n        return AgenticPlan::Final(tool_result::render(\n            command,\n            progress.run_outputs.last().map_or(\"\", String::as_str),\n            latest_user_text(messages).as_deref().unwrap_or_default(),\n        ));\n    }\n\n    if let Some(tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run) {\n        return plan_one(tool, json!({ \"command\": command }).to_string());\n    }\n\n    AgenticPlan::Final(format!(\n        \"I can run `{command}` when the client advertises a shell tool such as `bash`, `shell`, or `run_command`.\"\n    ))\n}\n\n/// A self-referential *generate → verify → final* recipe expressed as data.\n///\n/// Every self-inspection recipe (diagram, self-AST, self-heal, source-links,\n/// ledger, explain, change-request, repair-strategy, rebuild, question-catalog,\n/// Google-Trends catalog, Google-Trends learning) has the *same* three-step shape:\n/// write a generated document to `path`, verify it by They differ only in the document they generate,\n/// so they are modelled as one struct and one planner\n/// ([`plan_document_recipe`]) rather than a dozen copy-pasted functions — the exact\n/// generalization the meta-algorithm is meant to embody.\npub(super) struct DocumentRecipe {\n    /// The workspace-relative path the generated document is written to.\n    pub(super) path: &'static str,\n    /// The generated Links Notation document (a pure function of committed state).\n    pub(super) document: String,\n    /// The sandbox-allowlisted command that reads the document back for verification.\n    pub(super) verify_command: String,\n    /// The inline final answer returned once the write and verify steps are done.\n    pub(super) final_answer: String,\n}\n\n/// Plan the next step of a [`DocumentRecipe`]: `write → verify → final`. Steps whose\n/// capability the CLI did not advertise (or the conversation already satisfied) are\n/// skipped, so the loop adapts to whatever subset of tools a given CLI exposes.\npub(super) fn plan_document_recipe(\n    messages: &[ChatMessage],\n    tool_names: &[&str],\n    recipe: DocumentRecipe,\n) -> AgenticPlan {\n    let progress = Progress::scan(messages);\n\n    // Step 1: write the generated document.\n    if let Some(tool) =\n        tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Write).filter(|_| !progress.done(Capability::Write))\n    {\n        return plan_one(tool, write_arguments(recipe.path, &recipe.document));\n    }\n    // Step 2: verify by reading the document back.\n    if let Some(tool) =\n        tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run).filter(|_| !progress.done(Capability::Run))\n    {\n        return plan_one(\n            tool,\n            json!({ \"command\": recipe.verify_command }).to_string(),\n        );\n    }\n    // Step 3: nothing left to do — answer with the generated document inline.\n    AgenticPlan::Final(recipe.final_answer)\n}\n\n// State machine: web_search → web_fetch → write_file(formalize) → run_command(verify) → final.\nfn plan_formalization_step(messages: &[ChatMessage], tool_names: &[&str]) -> AgenticPlan {\n    let search_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Search);\n    let fetch_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Fetch);\n    let write_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Write);\n    let run_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run);\n\n    let progress = // Step 5: nothing left to do — answer with the knowledge base inline.\n    AgenticPlan::Final(final_answer(&formalized))\n}\n\n/// The issue-#538 recipe: search → fetch (Wikidata lexemes) → write the Checked\n    // before the sibling catalog recipe because both legitimately name \"Google Trends\";\n    // its keywords (\"learning frontier\", \"self-improvement loop\", \"cannot … resolve\") are\n    // disjoint from the catalog recipe's (prompt/answer/catalog/test), so ordering only\n    // guards a request that somehow names both.\n    if google_trends_learning::is_google_trends_learning_task(&task) {\n        return Some(plan_google_trends_learning_step(messages, tool_names));\n    }\n    if google_trends_catalog::is_google_trends_catalog_task(&task) {\n        return Some(plan_google_trends_catalog_step(messages, tool_names));\n    }\n    // The question-catalog recipe (issue #527): enumerate every possible question\n    // smallest-first, classify each grammatically and logically, and answer the\n    // meaningful ones. Checked alongside the other self-referential recipes and before\n    // formalization, since its request legitimately names \"Links Notation\" as the output\n    // format its catalog is rendered in. Its keywords (\"question catalog\", \"all possible\n    // questions\", …) are disjoint from the sibling recipes', so ordering only guards a\n    // request that somehow names both.\n    if question_catalog::is_question_catalog_task(&task) {\n        return Some(plan_question_catalog_step(messages, tool_names));\n    }\n    // Agent-mode counterpart of the web UI's report action (issues #687 + #822).\n    // This is a conversation state machine: after the initial report intent it\n    // continues across structured tool results or plain-text user choices.\n    if let Some(plan) = report_issue::plan_report_flow(messages, tool_names) {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    if let Some(answer) = conversation_recall::recall_answer_for(messages) {\n        return Some(AgenticPlan::Final(answer));\n    }\n    if let Some(answer) = tool_result::follow_up_answer(messages, &task) {\n        return Some(AgenticPlan::Final(answer));\n    }\n    if let Some(answer) = web_research::contextual_reference_clarification(&task) {\n        return Some(AgenticPlan::Final(answer));\n    }\n    if web_research::is_definition_followup(&task) {\n        if let Some(query) = web_research::definition_followup_topic(messages, &task) {\n            if let Some(plan) = web_research::plan_web_research_step(messages, tool_names, &query) {\n                return Some(plan);\n            }\n        } else {\n            return Some(AgenticPlan::Final(\n                web_research::definition_followup_clarification(&task),\n            ));\n        }\n    }\n    if let Some(plan) = intent_router::plan_edit_step(&task, messages, tool_names) {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    // Preserve the established stateful list/read recipe whenever the client\n    // exposes its typed read capability. The shared read-many route remains\n    // available for CLIs that advertise only a batch reader.\n    if tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Read).is_some() {\n        if let Some(file_task) = file_read_task_for(&task) {\n            return Some(plan_file_read_step(&file_task, messages, tool_names));\n        }\n    }\n    // A meanings-driven explicit local scope dominates generic search verbs.\n    // This state machine observes each result and widens only after emptiness.\n    if let Some(plan) = local_search::plan_local_search_step(messages, tool_names) {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    if let Some(plan) = comparison::plan_comparison_step(&task, messages, tool_names) {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    if let Some(plan) = capability_router::plan_shared_capability_step(&task, messages, tool_names)\n    {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    if let Some(command) = shell_command::shell_command_for_task(&task) {\n        if let Some(plan) = shell_file_fallback::plan_step(&task, messages, tool_names, &command) {\n            return Some(plan);\n        }\n        return Some(plan_shell_step(messages, tool_names, &command));\n    }\n    if let Some(file_task) = file_read_task_for(&task) {\n        return Some(plan_file_read_step(&file_task, messages, tool_names));\n    }\n    if is_formalization_task(&task) {\n        return Some(plan_formalization_step(messages, tool_names));\n    }\n    if meaning_detail::is_meaning_detail_task(&task) {\n        return Some(plan_meaning_detail_step(&task, messages, tool_names));\n    }\n    if diagram::is_diagram_task(&task) {\n        return Some(plan_diagram_step(messages, tool_names));\n    }\n    // A typed URL object is more specific than broad research prose. Resolve it\n    // before the research recipe so requests such as \"tell me about URL\" fetch\n    // that page instead of turning the URL itself into a search query.\n    if let Some(plan) = intent_router::plan_web_fetch_step(&task, messages, tool_names) {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    if let Some(query) = web_research::web_research_query_for(messages) {\n        if let Some(plan) = web_research::plan_web_research_step(messages, tool_names, &query) {\n            return Some(plan);\n        }\n    }\n    if let Some(plan) = intent_router::plan_web_search_step(&task, messages, tool_names) {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    // A generic localized \"find\" cue can describe either an open-web lookup or\n    // a workspace grep. The research routers above get first refusal whenever\n    // the client exposes their tools; explicit local/repository searches were\n    // already claimed by the capability router. This fallback therefore keeps\n    // grep available to grep-only clients without letting an alphabetically\n    // earlier local tool steal a web-research request.\n    if !tool_result::has_latest_turn_result(messages) {\n        if let Some(query) = shell_command::code_search_query_for_task(&task) {\n            if let Some(tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Grep) {\n                return Some(plan_one(\n                    tool,\n                    json!({ \"query\": query, \"pattern\": query }).to_string(),\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    if web_research::has_successful_search_result(messages) {\n        if let Some(query) = web_research::unresolved_web_research_query_for(messages) {\n            if let Some(plan) = web_research::plan_web_research_step(messages, tool_names, &query) {\n                return Some(plan);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    if let Some(answer) = tool_result::latest_turn_answer(messages, tool_names, &task) {\n        return Some(AgenticPlan::Final(answer));\n    }\n    if let Some(plan) = compose_general_change_plan(&task)\n        .map(|plan| plan_general_change_step(messages, tool_names, &plan))\n    {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    if let Some(query) = web_research::unresolved_web_research_query_for(messages) {\n        if let Some(plan) = web_research::plan_web_research_step(messages, tool_names, &query) {\n            return Some(plan);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Run a shell command through the client-owned tool loop, then present its result.\nfn plan_shell_step(messages: &[ChatMessage], tool_names: &[&str], command: &str) -> AgenticPlan {\n    let progress = Progress::scan(messages);\n    if progress.done(Capability::Run) {\n        return AgenticPlan::Final(tool_result::render(\n            command,\n            progress.run_outputs.last().map_or(\"\", String::as_str),\n            latest_user_text(messages).as_deref().unwrap_or_default(),\n        ));\n    }\n\n    if let Some(tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run) {\n        return plan_one(tool, json!({ \"command\": command }).to_string());\n    }\n\n    AgenticPlan::Final(format!(\n        \"I can run `{command}` when the client advertises a shell tool such as `bash`, `shell`, or `run_command`.\"\n    ))\n}\n\n/// A self-referential *generate → verify → final* recipe expressed as data.\n///\n/// Every self-inspection recipe (diagram, self-AST, self-heal, source-links,\n/// ledger, explain, change-request, repair-strategy, rebuild, question-catalog,\n/// Google-Trends catalog, Google-Trends learning) has the *same* three-step shape:\n/// write a generated document to `path`, verify it by running `verify_command`,\n/// then answer with `final_answer`. They differ only in the document they generate,\n/// so they are modelled as one struct and one planner\n/// ([`plan_document_recipe`]) rather than a dozen copy-pasted functions — the exact\n/// generalization the meta-algorithm is meant to embody.\npub(super) struct DocumentRecipe {\n    /// The workspace-relative path the generated document is written to.\n    pub(super) path: &'static str,\n    /// The generated Links Notation document (a pure function of committed state).\n    pub(super) document: String,\n    /// The sandbox-allowlisted command that reads the document back for verification.\n    pub(super) verify_command: String,\n    /// The inline final answer returned once the write and verify steps are done.\n    pub(super) final_answer: String,\n}\n\n/// Plan the next step of a [`DocumentRecipe`]: `write → verify → final`. Steps whose\n/// capability the CLI did not advertise (or the conversation already satisfied) are\n/// skipped, so the loop adapts to whatever subset of tools a given CLI exposes.\npub(super) fn plan_document_recipe(\n    messages: &[ChatMessage],\n    tool_names: &[&str],\n    recipe: DocumentRecipe,\n) -> AgenticPlan {\n    let progress = Progress::scan(messages);\n\n    // Step 1: write the generated document.\n    if let Some(tool) =\n        tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Write).filter(|_| !progress.done(Capability::Write))\n    {\n        return plan_one(tool, write_arguments(recipe.path, &recipe.document));\n    }\n    // Step 2: verify by reading the document back.\n    if let Some(tool) =\n        tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run).filter(|_| !progress.done(Capability::Run))\n    {\n        return plan_one(\n            tool,\n            json!({ \"command\": recipe.verify_command }).to_string(),\n        );\n    }\n    // Step 3: nothing left to do — answer with the generated document inline.\n    AgenticPlan::Final(recipe.final_answer)\n}\n\n// State machine: web_search → web_fetch → write_file(formalize) → run_command(verify) → final.\nfn plan_formalization_step(messages: &[ChatMessage], tool_names: &[&str]) -> AgenticPlan {\n    let search_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Search);\n    let fetch_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Fetch);\n    let write_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Write);\n    let run_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run);\n\n    let progress = Progress::scan(messages);\n\n    // Step 1: search for the source text.\n    if let Some(tool) = search_tool {\n        if !progress.done(Capability::Search) {\n            return plan_one(tool, json!({ \"query\": SEARCH_QUERY }).to_string());\n        }\n    }\n    // Step 2: fetch the source text.\n    if let Some(tool) = fetch_tool {\n        if !progress.done(Capability::Fetch) {\n            return plan_one(tool, fetch_arguments(CANONICAL_SOURCE_URL));\n        }\n    }\n\n    // The source text for the knowledge base: the latest non-errored fetch result\n    // if we have one, else the canonical synopsis (the determinism fallback).\n    let source = progress\n        .fetched_text\n        .as_deref()\n        .unwrap_or(CANONICAL_FISHERMAN_SYNOPSIS);\n    let formalized = formalize_text_to_links(source, \"\");\n\n    // Step 3: write the formalized knowledge base.\n    if let Some(tool) = write_tool {\n        if !progress.done(Capability::Write) {\n            return plan_one(tool, write_arguments(KB_PATH, &formalized.links_notation));\n        }\n    }\n    // Step 4: verify by reading the file back.\n    if let Some(tool) = run_tool {\n        if // Step 5: nothing left to do — answer with the knowledge base inline.\n    AgenticPlan::Final(final_answer(&formalized))\n}\n\n/// The issue-#538 recipe: search → fetch (Wikidata lexemes) → write the Agentic CLIs disagree on the parameter name — the in-repo driver\n/// reads `path`, the `@link-assistant/agent` CLI's `write` tool wants `filePath`,\n/// others use `file_path`. tool loop, then present its result.\nfn plan_shell_step(messages: &[ChatMessage], tool_names: &[&str], command: &str) -> AgenticPlan {\n    let progress = Progress::scan(messages);\n    if progress.done(Capability::Run) {\n        return AgenticPlan::Final(tool_result::render(\n            command,\n            progress.run_outputs.last().map_or(\"\", String::as_str),\n            latest_user_text(messages).as_deref().unwrap_or_default(),\n        ));\n    }\n\n    if let Some(tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run) {\n        return plan_one(tool, json!({ \"command\": command }).to_string());\n    }\n\n    AgenticPlan::Final(format!(\n        \"I can run `{command}` when the client advertises a shell tool such as `bash`, `shell`, or `run_command`.\"\n    ))\n}\n\n/// A self-referential *generate → verify → final* recipe expressed as data.\n///\n/// Every self-inspection recipe (diagram, self-AST, self-heal, source-links,\n/// ledger, explain, change-request, repair-strategy, rebuild, question-catalog,\n/// Google-Trends catalog, Google-Trends learning) has the *same* three-step shape:\n/// write a generated document to `path`, verify it by running `verify_command`,\n/// then answer with `final_answer`. They differ only in the document they generate,\n/// so they are modelled as one struct and one planner\n/// ([`plan_document_recipe`]) rather than a dozen copy-pasted functions — the exact\n/// generalization the meta-algorithm is meant to embody.\npub(super) struct DocumentRecipe {\n    /// The workspace-relative path the generated document is written to.\n    pub(super) path: &'static str,\n    /// The generated Links Notation document (a pure function of committed state).\n    pub(super) document: String,\n    /// The sandbox-allowlisted command that reads the document back for verification.\n    pub(super) verify_command: String,\n    /// The inline final answer returned once the write and verify steps are done.\n    pub(super) final_answer: String,\n}\n\n/// Plan the next step of a [`DocumentRecipe`]: `write → verify → final`. Steps whose\n/// capability the CLI did not advertise (or the conversation already satisfied) are\n/// skipped, so the loop adapts to whatever subset of tools a given CLI exposes.\npub(super) fn plan_document_recipe(\n    messages: &[ChatMessage],\n    tool_names: &[&str],\n    recipe: DocumentRecipe,\n) -> AgenticPlan {\n    let progress = Progress::scan(messages);\n\n    // Step 1: write the generated document.\n    if let Some(tool) =\n        tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Write).filter(|_| !progress.done(Capability::Write))\n    {\n        return plan_one(tool, write_arguments(recipe.path, &recipe.document));\n    }\n    // Step 2: verify by reading the document back.\n    if let Some(tool) =\n        tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run).filter(|_| !progress.done(Capability::Run))\n    {\n        return plan_one(\n            tool,\n            json!({ \"command\": recipe.verify_command }).to_string(),\n        );\n    }\n    // Step 3: nothing left to do — answer with the generated document inline.\n    AgenticPlan::Final(recipe.final_answer)\n}\n\n// State machine: web_search → web_fetch → write_file(formalize) → run_command(verify) → final.\nfn plan_formalization_step(messages: &[ChatMessage], tool_names: &[&str]) -> AgenticPlan {\n    let search_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Search);\n    let fetch_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Fetch);\n    let write_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Write);\n    let run_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run);\n\n    let progress = Progress::scan(messages);\n\n    // Step 1: search for the source text.\n    if let Some(tool) = search_tool {\n        if !progress.done(Capability::Search) {\n            return plan_one(tool, json!({ \"query\": SEARCH_QUERY }).to_string());\n        }\n    }\n    // Step 2: fetch the source text.\n    if let Some(tool) = fetch_tool {\n        if !progress.done(Capability::Fetch) {\n            return plan_one(tool, fetch_arguments(CANONICAL_SOURCE_URL));\n        }\n    }\n\n    // The source text for the knowledge base: the latest non-errored fetch result\n    // if we have one, else the canonical synopsis (the determinism fallback).\n    let source = progress\n        .fetched_text\n        .as_deref()\n        .unwrap_or(CANONICAL_FISHERMAN_SYNOPSIS);\n    let formalized = formalize_text_to_links(source, \"\");\n\n    // Step 3: write the formalized knowledge base.\n    if let Some(tool) = write_tool {\n        if !progress.done(Capability::Write) {\n            return plan_one(tool, write_arguments(KB_PATH, &formalized.links_notation));\n        }\n    }\n    // Step 4: verify by reading the file back.\n    if let Some(tool) = run_tool {\n        if !progress.done(Capability::Run) {\n            let arguments = json!({ \"command\": format!(\"cat {KB_PATH}\") });\n            return plan_one(tool, arguments.to_string());\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Step 5: nothing left to do — answer with the knowledge base inline.\n    AgenticPlan::Final(final_answer(&formalized))\n}\n\n/// The issue-#538 recipe: search → fetch (Wikidata lexemes) → write the Steps whose tool the CLI did\n/// not advertise are skipped.\nfn plan_meaning_detail_step(\n    task: &str,\n    messages: &[ChatMessage],\n    tool_names: &[&str],\n) -> AgenticPlan {\n    // Route to the concept the request names (default: tomato — the canonical task).\n    let concept = meaning_detail::concept_for_task(task).unwrap_or(&meaning_detail::TOMATO);\n\n    let search_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Search);\n    let fetch_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Fetch);\n    let write_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Write);\n    let run_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run);\n\n    let progress = Progress::scan(messages);\n\n    // Step 1: search for the Wikidata lexeme data.\n    if let Some(tool) = search_tool {\n        if !progress.done(Capability::Search) {\n            return plan_one(tool, json!({ \"query\": concept.search_query }).to_string());\n        }\n    }\n    // Step 2: fetch the lexeme forms (where the missing plural is recovered).\n    if let Some(tool) = fetch_tool {\n        if !progress.done(Capability::Fetch) {\n            return plan_one(tool, fetch_arguments(concept.source_url));\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Re-derive the enriched block from the fetched lexeme facts (or the canonical\n    // fallback when the fetch errored), exactly as the formalization recipe does.\n    let block = meaning_detail::enrich_block(concept, progress.fetched_text.as_deref());\n\n    // Step 3: write the enriched meaning block.\n    if let Some(tool) = write_tool {\n        if !progress.done(Capability::Write) {\n            return plan_one(tool, write_arguments(concept.kb_path, &block));\n        }\n    }\n    // Step 4: verify by reading the enriched block back (mirrors the formalization\n    // recipe; non-errored fetch result, else the\n    // canonical synopsis (the determinism fallback).\n    let source = inline_source\n        .as_deref()\n        .or(progress.fetched_text.as_deref())\n        .unwrap_or(CANONICAL_FISHERMAN_SYNOPSIS);\n    let formalized = formalize_text_to_links(source, \"\");\n\n    // Step 3: write the formalized knowledge base.\n    if let Some(tool) = write_tool {\n back.\n    if let Some(tool) = run_tool {\n        if !progress.done(Capability::Run) {\n            let arguments = json!({ \"command\": format!(\"cat {KB_PATH}\") });\n            return plan_one(tool, arguments.to_string());\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Step 5: nothing left to do — answer with the knowledge base inline.\n    AgenticPlan::Final(final_answer(&formalized))\n}\n\n/// The The shared read-many route remains\n    // available for CLIs that advertise only a batch reader.\n    if tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Read).is_some() {\n        if let Some(file_task) = file_read_task_for(&task) {\n            return Some(plan_file_read_step(&file_task, messages, tool_names));\n        }\n    }\n    // A meanings-driven explicit local scope dominates generic search verbs.\n    // This state machine observes each result and widens only after emptiness.\n    if let Some(plan) = local_search::plan_local_search_step(messages, tool_names) {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    if let Some(plan) = comparison::plan_comparison_step(&task, messages, tool_names) {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    if let Some(plan) = capability_router::plan_shared_capability_step(&task, messages, tool_names)\n    {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    if let Some(command) = shell_command::shell_command_for_task(&task) {\n        if let Some(plan) = shell_file_fallback::plan_step(&task, messages, tool_names, &command) {\n            return Some(plan);\n        }\n        return Some(plan_shell_step(messages, tool_names, &command));\n    }\n    if let Some(file_task) = file_read_task_for(&task) {\n        return Some(plan_file_read_step(&file_task, messages, tool_names));\n    }\n    if is_formalization_task(&task) {\n        return Some(plan_formalization_step(&task, messages, tool_names));\n    }\n    if meaning_detail::is_meaning_detail_task(&task) {\n        return Some(plan_meaning_detail_step(&task, messages, tool_names));\n    }\n    if diagram::is_diagram_task(&task) {\n        return Some(plan_diagram_step(messages, tool_names));\n    }\n    // A typed URL object is more specific than broad research prose. Resolve it\n    // before the research recipe so requests such as \"tell me about URL\" fetch\n    // that page instead of turning the URL itself into a search query.\n    if let Some(plan) = intent_router::plan_web_fetch_step(&task, messages, tool_names) {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    if let Some(query) = web_research::web_research_query_for(messages) {\n        if let Some(plan) = web_research::plan_web_research_step(messages, tool_names, &query) {\n            return Some(plan);\n        }\n    }\n    if let Some(plan) = intent_router::plan_web_search_step(&task, messages, tool_names) {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    // A generic localized \"find\" cue can describe either an open-web lookup or\n    // a workspace grep. The research routers above get first refusal whenever\n    // the client exposes their tools; explicit local/repository searches were\n    // already claimed by the capability router. This fallback therefore keeps\n    // grep available to grep-only clients without letting an alphabetically\n    // earlier local tool steal a web-research request.\n    if !tool_result::has_latest_turn_result(messages) {\n        if let Some(query) = shell_command::code_search_query_for_task(&task) {\n            if let Some(tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Grep) {\n                return Some(plan_one(\n                    tool,\n                    json!({ \"query\": query, \"pattern\": query }).to_string(),\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    if web_research::has_successful_search_result(messages) {\n        if let Some(query) = web_research::unresolved_web_research_query_for(messages) {\n            if let Some(plan) = web_research::plan_web_research_step(messages, tool_names, &query) {\n                return Some(plan);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    if let Some(answer) = tool_result::latest_turn_answer(messages, tool_names, &task) {\n        return Some(AgenticPlan::Final(answer));\n    }\n    if let Some(plan) = compose_general_change_plan(&task)\n        .map(|plan| plan_general_change_step(messages, tool_names, &plan))\n    {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    if let Some(query) = web_research::unresolved_web_research_query_for(messages) {\n        if let Some(plan) = web_research::plan_web_research_step(messages, tool_names, &query) {\n            return Some(plan);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Run a shell command through the client-owned tool loop, then present its result.\nfn plan_shell_step(messages: &[ChatMessage], tool_names: &[&str], command: &str) -> AgenticPlan {\n    let progress = Progress::scan(messages);\n    if progress.done(Capability::Run) {\n        return AgenticPlan::Final(tool_result::render(\n            command,\n            progress.run_outputs.last().map_or(\"\", String::as_str),\n            latest_user_text(messages).as_deref().unwrap_or_default(),\n        ));\n    }\n\n    if let Some(tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run) {\n        return plan_one(tool, json!({ \"command\": command }).to_string());\n    }\n\n    AgenticPlan::Final(format!(\n        \"I can run `{command}` when the client advertises a shell tool such as `bash`, `shell`, or `run_command`.\"\n    ))\n}\n\n/// A self-referential *generate → verify → final* recipe expressed as data.\n///\n/// Every self-inspection recipe (diagram, self-AST, self-heal, source-links,\n/// ledger, explain, change-request, repair-strategy, rebuild, question-catalog,\n/// Google-Trends catalog, Google-Trends learning) has the *same* three-step shape:\n/// write a generated document to `path`, verify it by running `verify_command`,\n/// then answer with `final_answer`. They differ only in the document they generate,\n/// so they are modelled as one struct and one planner\n/// ([`plan_document_recipe`]) rather than a dozen copy-pasted functions — the exact\n/// generalization the meta-algorithm is meant to embody.\npub(super) struct DocumentRecipe {\n    /// The workspace-relative path the generated document is written to.\n    pub(super) path: &'static str,\n    /// The generated Links Notation document (a pure function of committed state).\n    pub(super) document: String,\n    /// The sandbox-allowlisted command that reads the document back for verification.\n    pub(super) verify_command: String,\n    /// The inline final answer returned once the write and verify steps are done.\n    pub(super) final_answer: String,\n}\n\n/// Plan the next step of a [`DocumentRecipe`]: `write → verify → final`. Steps whose\n/// capability the CLI did not advertise (or the conversation already satisfied) are\n/// skipped, so the loop adapts to whatever subset of tools a given CLI exposes.\npub(super) fn plan_document_recipe(\n    messages: &[ChatMessage],\n    tool_names: &[&str],\n    recipe: DocumentRecipe,\n) -> AgenticPlan {\n    let progress = Progress::scan(messages);\n\n    // Step 1: write the generated document.\n    if let Some(tool) =\n        tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Write).filter(|_| !progress.done(Capability::Write))\n    {\n        return plan_one(tool, write_arguments(recipe.path, &recipe.document));\n    }\n    // Step 2: verify by reading the document back.\n    if let Some(tool) =\n        tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run).filter(|_| !progress.done(Capability::Run))\n    {\n        return plan_one(\n            tool,\n            json!({ \"command\": recipe.verify_command }).to_string(),\n        );\n    }\n    // Step 3: nothing left to do — answer with the generated document inline.\n    AgenticPlan::Final(recipe.final_answer)\n}\n\n// State machine: web_search → web_fetch → write_file(formalize) → run_command(verify) → final.\nfn plan_formalization_step(\n    task: &str,\n    messages: &[ChatMessage],\n    tool_names: &[&str],\n) -> AgenticPlan {\n    let write_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Write);\n    let run_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run);\n\n    let progress = Progress::scan(messages);\n\n    // A task that quotes its own source text carries the document inline, so\n    // searching inline_source.is_none() {\n        // Step 1: search for the source text.\n        if let Some(tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Search) {\n            if !progress.done(Capability::Search) {\n                return plan_one(tool, json!({ \"query\": SEARCH_QUERY }).to_string());\n            }\n        }\n        // Step 2: fetch the source text.\n        if let Some(tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Fetch) {\n            if !progress.done(Capability::Fetch) {\n                return plan_one(tool, fetch_arguments(CANONICAL_SOURCE_URL));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // The source text for the knowledge base: the text quoted in the task if\n    // there is one, else the latest non-errored fetch result, else the\n    // canonical synopsis (the // Step 5: nothing left to do — answer with the knowledge base inline.\n    AgenticPlan::Final(final_answer(&formalized))\n}\n\n/// The issue-#538 recipe: search → fetch (Wikidata lexemes) → write the Mirrors the formalization recipe but re-derives\n/// the enriched meaning block from the fetched lexeme facts instead of formalizing\n/// prose. The concept to enrich is routed from the request itself\n/// ([`meaning_detail::concept_for_task`]), so the *same* recipe makes tomato,\n/// potato, or any registered concept more detailed. Steps whose tool the CLI did\n/// not advertise are skipped.\nfn plan_meaning_detail_step(\n    task: &str,\n    messages: &[ChatMessage],\n    tool_names: &[&str],\n) -> AgenticPlan {\n    // Route to the concept the request names (default: tomato — the canonical task).\n    let concept = meaning_detail::concept_for_task(task).unwrap_or(&meaning_detail::TOMATO);\n\n    let search_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Search);\n    let fetch_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Fetch);\n    let write_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Write);\n    let run_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run);\n\n    let progress = Progress::scan(messages);\n\n    // Step 1: search for the Wikidata lexeme data.\n    if let Some(tool) = search_tool {\n        if !progress.done(Capability::Search) {\n            return plan_one(tool, json!({ \"query\": concept.search_query }).to_string());\n        }\n    }\n    // Step 2: fetch the lexeme forms (where the missing plural is recovered).\n    if let Some(tool) = fetch_tool {\n        if !progress.done(Capability::Fetch) {\n            return plan_one(tool, fetch_arguments(concept.source_url));\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Re-derive the enriched block from the fetched lexeme facts (or the canonical\n    // fallback when the fetch errored), exactly as the formalization recipe does.\n    let block = meaning_detail::enrich_block(concept, progress.fetched_text.as_deref());\n\n    // Step 3: write the enriched meaning block.\n    if let Some(tool) = write_tool {\n        if !progress.done(Capability::Write) {\n            return plan_one(tool, write_arguments(concept.kb_path, &block));\n        }\n    }\n    // Step 4: verify by reading the enriched block back (mirrors the formalization\n    // recipe; `cat` is the allowlisted read the sandbox workspace supports).\n    if let Some(tool) = run_tool {\n        if !progress.done(Capability::Run) {\n            let arguments = json!({ \"command\": format!(\"cat {}\", concept.kb_path) });\n            return plan_one(tool, arguments.to_string());\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Step 5: nothing left to do — answer with the enriched block inline.\n    AgenticPlan::Final(meaning_detail::final_answer_for(concept, &block))\n}\n\n/// The issue-#538 diagram recipe: write the generated mermaid document → verify →\n/// final. Steps whose tool the CLI did not advertise are\n/// skipped.\nfn plan_ledger_step(messages: &[ChatMessage], tool_names: &[&str]) -> AgenticPlan {\n    let document = ledger::render_document();\n    let final_answer = ledger::final_answer(&document);\n    plan_document_recipe(\n        messages,\n        tool_names,\n        DocumentRecipe {\n            path: ledger::LEDGER_PATH,\n            verify_command: format!(\"cat {}\", ledger::LEDGER_PATH),\n            final_answer,\n            document,\n        },\n    )\n}\n\n/// The issue-#558 self-explanation recipe: write the generated grounded-explanation\n/// document → verify → final. Capability::Grep) {\n                return Some(plan_one(\n                    tool,\n                    json!({ \"query\": query, \"pattern\": query }).to_string(),\n                ));\n Some(plan) = web_research::plan_web_research_step(messages, tool_names, &query) {\n                return Some(plan);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    if let Some(answer) = tool_result::latest_turn_answer(messages, tool_names, &task) {\n        return Some(AgenticPlan::Final(answer));\n    }\n    if let Some(plan) = compose_general_change_plan(&task)\n        .map(|plan| plan_general_change_step(messages, tool_names, &plan))\n    {\n        return Some(plan);\n    }\n    if let Some(query) = web_research::unresolved_web_research_query_for(messages) {\n        if let The\nwhole session — advertised as a Formal-AI-driven run — was actually driven\nby a free neural model; the Formal AI server never received the traffic.\n\nThis is not fixable inside formal-ai: the defect is in the external\n`@link-assistant/agent` CLI, which detects the parsing failure, prints\nCRITICAL, and then **continues with the wrong model** instead of aborting.\nThe generalizing fix is fail-fast: an explicitly requested model that cannot\nbe honored must terminate the run with a non-zero exit code. Issue #956 is the concrete\ninstance — a custom formalization task had its quoted source text silently\ndiscarded in favour of the seeded fairy tale. This PR fixes both legs:\n\n- the formalization recipe honors inline-quoted source text\n  (`src/agentic_coding/formalization_recipe.rs`), and\n- `FORMAL_AI_TRACE_REQUESTS=1` now traces `agentic_task` and\n  `formalization_source` routing decisions, so an empty run can be\n  diagnosed from its log instead of guessed at.\n\nThe restart-budget half of the loop (don't resume a run that changed\nnothing without bounding retries) is Hive-Mind-side work, tracked as R-B3\nin hive-mind #2146.\n\n### Defect C — final-message markdown collapses in GitHub comments (R1c)\n\nThe logs show `lino` knowledge-base text and plan events emitted as bare\nindented text, which GitHub comments re-flow into prose. Fixed in this PR:\n`issue_report::fenced_block` wraps every machine-text emitter (general-change\nplan event, formalized knowledge base, report exports) in fenced code blocks,\nwith regression tests in `tests/unit/issue_996_markdown.rs`. The related\ngoal-preamble echo was already fixed by #904."

The requested model\n> will NOT be used — the default model will be used instead.`\n\nLine 485 confirms the substitution: `\"modelID\": \"minimax-m2.5-free\"`. The\nwhole session — advertised as a Formal-AI-driven run — was actually driven\nby a free neural model; the Formal AI server never received the traffic.\n\nThis is not fixable inside formal-ai: the defect is in the external\n`@link-assistant/agent` CLI, which detects the parsing failure, prints\nCRITICAL, and then **continues with the wrong model** instead of aborting.\nThe generalizing fix is fail-fast: an explicitly requested model that cannot\nbe honored must terminate the run with a non-zero exit code. Issue #956 is the concrete\ninstance — a custom formalization task had its quoted source text silently\ndiscarded in favour of the seeded fairy tale. This PR fixes both legs:\n\n- the formalization recipe honors inline-quoted source text\n  (`src/agentic_coding/formalization_recipe.rs`), and\n- `FORMAL_AI_TRACE_REQUESTS=1` now traces `agentic_task` and\n  `formalization_source` routing decisions, so an empty run can be\n  diagnosed from its log instead of guessed at.\n\nThe restart-budget half of the loop (don't resume a run that changed\nnothing without bounding retries) is Hive-Mind-side work, tracked as R-B3\nin hive-mind #2146.\n\n### Defect C — final-message markdown collapses in GitHub comments (R1c)\n\nThe logs show `lino` knowledge-base text and plan events emitted as bare\nindented text, which GitHub comments re-flow into prose. The lesson for Formal AI: the\n  self-coding loop does not need a finished toolbox up front; it needs a\n  reliable start-to-end loop plus the ability to extend itself mid-run,\n  which is exactly the gap the PhU3X2/8GWnaH logs expose (R1b).\n- [OpenHands](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands) (MIT-licensed,\n  ex-OpenDevin) executes plans as code actions in a sandboxed Docker\n  environment and iterates on test results — the same\n  execute-verify-iterate contract CONTRIBUTING.md already mandates for the\n  in-repo agentic driver.\n- [SWE-agent](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent) introduced the\n  Agent-Computer Interface: a small, stable command surface an agent can\n  reliably drive. Formal AI's OpenAI-compatible `serve` boundary plus the\n  external `@link-assistant/agent` CLI is this project's ACI; keeping it\n  small and deterministic is what makes symbolic self-coding testable.\n- [SWE-EVO (arXiv:2512.18470)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.18470) and\n  [SWE-Chain (arXiv:2605.14415)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.14415)\n  benchmark long-horizon, multi-step evolution — evidence that \"one issue,\n  one PR, every requirement\" (R11) is measured industry-wide as chained\n  end-to-end completion, not single-patch success.\n\n## Upstream reports and new-component proposals (R5, R6)\n\n_(filled in below)_\n",

This is likely a\n> Bun/yargs argument parsing bug (oven-sh/bun#22157). The requested model\n> will NOT be used — the default model will be used instead.`\n\nLine 485 confirms the substitution: `\"modelID\": \"minimax-m2.5-free\"`. The\nwhole session — advertised as a Formal-AI-driven run — was actually driven\nby a free neural model; the Formal AI server never received the traffic.\n\nThis is not fixable inside formal-ai: the defect is in the external\n`@link-assistant/agent` CLI, which detects the parsing failure, prints\nCRITICAL, and then **continues with the wrong model** instead of aborting.\nThe generalizing fix is fail-fast: an explicitly requested model that cannot\nbe honored must terminate the run with a non-zero exit code. See \"Upstream\nreports\" below for the report filed against `link-assistant/agent`.\n\n### Defect B — runs that end with zero code changes (R1b)\n\n`raw-data/hive-mind-log-PhU3X2-sanitized.log.txt` line 723 shows the\nassistant (this time genuinely `\"model\": \"formal-ai\"`) answering a coding\ntask with conversational filler:\n\n> `Let me run a quick command to get that for you.`\n\n— no tool call follows, the run produces no code changes, and lines\n1068–1091 show Hive Mind reacting with its auto-restart/resume loop.\n`hive-mind-log-8GWnaH-sanitized.log.txt` records a second session with the\nsame shape.\n\nRoot cause on the Formal-AI side: a received `--task` that did not match a\nrecipe fell through to chat-style canned responses, and there was no\nvisibility into how the task was routed. Issue #956 is the concrete\ninstance — a custom formalization task had its quoted source text silently\ndiscarded in favour of the seeded fairy tale. This PR fixes both legs:\n\n- the formalization recipe honors inline-quoted source text\n  (`src/agentic_coding/formalization_recipe.rs`), and\n- `FORMAL_AI_TRACE_REQUESTS=1` now traces `agentic_task` and\n  `formalization_source` routing decisions, so an empty run can be\n  diagnosed from its log instead of guessed at.\n\nThe restart-budget half of the loop (don't resume a run that changed\nnothing without bounding retries) is Hive-Mind-side work, tracked as R-B3\nin hive-mind #2146.\n\n### Defect C — final-message markdown collapses in GitHub comments (R1c)\n\nThe logs show `lino` knowledge-base text and plan events emitted as bare\nindented text, which GitHub comments re-flow into prose. Fixed in this PR:\n`issue_report::fenced_block` wraps every machine-text emitter (general-change\nplan event, formalized knowledge base, report exports) in fenced code blocks,\nwith regression tests in `tests/unit/issue_996_markdown.rs`. The related\ngoal-preamble echo was already fixed by #904.\n\n## Most critical open issues and what this PR closes (R2, R3)\n\n`raw-data/github/open-issues.json` and `open-prs.json` snapshot the queue at\nanalysis time. The lesson for Formal AI: the\n  self-coding loop does not need a finished toolbox up front; it needs a\n  reliable start-to-end loop plus the ability to extend itself mid-run,\n  which is exactly the gap the PhU3X2/8GWnaH logs expose (R1b).\n- [OpenHands](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands) (MIT-licensed,\n  ex-OpenDevin) executes plans as code actions in a sandboxed Docker\n  environment and iterates on test results — the same\n  execute-verify-iterate contract CONTRIBUTING.md already mandates for the\n  in-repo agentic driver.\n- [SWE-agent](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent) introduced the\n  Agent-Computer Interface: a small, stable command surface an agent can\n  reliably drive. Formal AI's OpenAI-compatible `serve` boundary plus the\n  external `@link-assistant/agent` CLI is this project's ACI; keeping it\n  small and deterministic is what makes symbolic self-coding testable.\n- [SWE-EVO (arXiv:2512.18470)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.18470) and\n  [SWE-Chain (arXiv:2605.14415)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.14415)\n  benchmark long-horizon, multi-step evolution — evidence that \"one issue,\n  one PR, every requirement\" (R11) is measured industry-wide as chained\n  end-to-end completion, not single-patch success.\n\n## Upstream reports and new-component proposals (R5, R6)\n\n_(filled in below)_\n",
